authority.note: Engineer-authored derivation mechanics. Specifications and their requirement sets are Planner-owned (AGENTS.md I2 origin gating); nothing here creates a row, plan, or WorkRequest.

derived_from.record_title: R2: Cross-System High-Leverage Next Steps Synthesis (Repo, Pending WRs, PRs #1006-#1017, Migrations V186-V221, and Forum/Transcripts)

captured_state.method: read-only: conduit GET /state, nebula-srv REST, psql SELECT against nexus (pguser, search_path per service)
analyst_claims_not_reverified_here: 19 compiled WorkRequest drafts / 8 intent cards awaiting ratification (Planner package 3dd1987d)
7 thallium-* services probing UP while manifest says OFFLINE
36/102 Terrain services unbound to canonical assets; stage-0 mapping scored 0/25 at sim >= 0.8

type_gaps.title: No Specification can group Requirements
type_gaps.evidence: resolution.specification = 0 rows; its shape requires agenda_id NOT NULL and a single requirement_id, so it is a per-agenda revision of one requirement, not a container. nebula.spec_requirements = 0 rows and its spec_id FK targets nebula.spec_documents_history (a document table), not a specification grouping. nebula.specifications is a view over 2 history rows (1 current, an agenda 'probe').
type_gaps.consequence: A derived Specification (goal + N requirements) has no table, no id, and no membership edge to write to.

type_gaps.title: The live Requirement surface is not the one the link tables reference
type_gaps.evidence: nebula.requirements (view over nebula.requirements_history) holds the 27 in-use rows; resolution.requirement holds 0. V220's resolution.request_requirement_link FKs to resolution.requirement(id), so it cannot reference any live requirement.
type_gaps.consequence: Even if a link were authored it would be unwritable or dangling; the canonical landing (plan 8261650) canonicalized WorkRequests but not Requirements.

type_gaps.title: Blueprint → Requirement parentage is not representable through the authoring API
type_gaps.evidence: POST /api/plans writes nebula.blueprints_history with payload.spec_ref and payload.requirement_ref hardcoded to null (typescript/nebula-srv/src/routes.ts, blueprintPayload literal). No request field sets them, and no FK validates them. 4 of 54 blueprints happen to carry a resolvable requirement_ref (imported rows); the 5 pending blueprints carry empty refs.
type_gaps.consequence: 'For each Requirement, create a Blueprint' cannot be expressed: the blueprint is born parentless and the link is advisory JSON at best.

type_gaps.title: Requirement → WorkRequest provenance is unpopulated and its shortcut is gone
type_gaps.evidence: resolution.work_request = 50 rows, resolution.request_requirement_link = 0 rows. resolution.work_request.source_requirement_id no longer exists (V221 cutover), so the dropped shortcut left no backfilled link behind.
type_gaps.consequence: A WorkRequest compiled today cannot state which Requirement it implements; the chain breaks at the last hop.

type_gaps.title: Compilation binds a plan by column, not by Blueprint identity
type_gaps.evidence: POST /api/requirements/:id/compile optionally creates a Conduit plan and links it via UPDATE requirements SET conduit_plan_id (routes.ts). The Blueprint row (blueprints_history) is not part of that path, and no Specification context participates.
type_gaps.consequence: Requirement → plan exists; Requirement → Blueprint → WorkRequest does not. The two plan notions are joined only by plan_number convention.

type_gaps.title: There is no existing grouped-Requirement instance to imitate
type_gaps.evidence: 0 of 27 current requirements have parent_id set; req_type is null for 23 (4 Story). nebula.assess_ripple already traverses requirement parent/child hierarchy, so the traversal exists but has never had a tree.
type_gaps.consequence: The cheapest interim representation (Specification = Epic root with child Requirements) is available structurally but has zero precedent, and would be a convention rather than a type.

interim_convention_available.description: Specification as a root requirement with req_type='Epic' and Requirements as children via parent_id; Blueprint parentage carried in payload.requirement_ref.
interim_convention_available.limits: Convention only: no Specification identity, no goal/status lifecycle, no FK on blueprint parentage, and nothing prevents a childless or multi-parent tree.
interim_convention_available.recommended_for: unblocking one pilot Specification only, if the operator wants immediate authoring before the type work lands.

proposed_minimal_types.name: Specification container
proposed_minimal_types.shape: resolution.specification_set(id uuid PK, title, goal, status in (draft,ratified,retired), source_record_id uuid -> nebula.agent_records, system_id uuid NULL, valid_from/valid_until/recorded_on_dt/recorded_until_dt, created_at) with partial unique index on current rows; existing per-agenda rows renamed or viewed as specification_revision.
proposed_minimal_types.why: Named, goal-bearing grouping with its own lifecycle; does not overload the revision table.
proposed_minimal_types.open_question: Does the Architect's 'Specification' equal this container, or the revision artifact? Naming and ownership must be ratified before DDL.

proposed_minimal_types.name: Specification→Requirement membership
proposed_minimal_types.shape: resolution.specification_requirement(specification_id FK, requirement_id FK, ordinal int, role in (primary,supporting), valid_from/valid_until/recorded_on_dt/recorded_until_dt) with PK/unique on (specification_id, requirement_id) among current rows.
proposed_minimal_types.why: Makes 'grouped collection' a real edge with order, without duplicating requirement text.
proposed_minimal_types.open_question: Membership must target whichever requirement surface is declared canonical (see P4).

proposed_minimal_types.name: Blueprint parentage
proposed_minimal_types.shape: blueprints_history gains specification_id uuid NULL and requirement_id uuid NULL (FK-validated), populated by POST /api/plans from explicit request fields; payload refs become projections of the columns.
proposed_minimal_types.why: Turns the advisory JSON refs into an enforceable edge at authoring time.
proposed_minimal_types.open_question: Add columns (schema change) vs validate-then-write payload only (no schema change, weaker).

proposed_minimal_types.name: Single Requirement authority
proposed_minimal_types.shape: Either (a) port nebula.requirements_history rows into resolution.requirement identity-preserving and repoint nebula-srv, or (b) declare nebula.requirements canonical for the requirement layer and retarget V220's FK.
proposed_minimal_types.why: Every other edge depends on this; with two surfaces, links are either dangling or unrepresentable.
proposed_minimal_types.open_question: This is the load-bearing authority decision. (a) matches the Architect's declared target and V220; (b) is cheaper but contradicts the canonical landing.

proposed_minimal_types.name: Compile provenance
proposed_minimal_types.shape: On Requirement→plan compilation, insert resolution.request_requirement_link(request_id, requirement_id, relation='implements', provenance='compile:<receiptId>') in the same transaction as the plan link.
proposed_minimal_types.why: Closes the last hop and makes the chain auditable end to end.
proposed_minimal_types.open_question: Depends on P4 and on the WorkRequest TypeSpec contract question left open in 4fb5f9b4.

specifications.title: WorkRequest canonicalization is closed and provable
specifications.goal: Finish the residual ledger, replication and reader-proof work so the canonical WorkRequest landing can be depended on rather than merely declared complete.
specifications.outcome: V187 is ledgered, the four recent migrations are replicated to vanadium, and no consumer still depends on the dropped source_requirement shortcut.
specifications.source: Analyst R2 Tier 1 (steps 1A-1C), re-verified: plan 8261650 is completed; V219/V220/V221 are ledgered; V187 is not.
specifications.scope_boundary: Documentary ledger row, replication evidence and reader audits only. No schema change, no data repair, no new canonical surface.

requirements.title: Ledger V187
requirements.outcome: resolution.migration_ledger contains exactly one documentary row for V187__work_request_view_demotion.
acceptance_criteria: SELECT count(*) FROM resolution.migration_ledger WHERE migration_label LIKE 'V187%' returns 1.
The row names the merge commit, the observed apply window, and states that the apply predates the ledger entry.
The change performs no schema or data mutation beyond the ledger INSERT, and is idempotent (WHERE NOT EXISTS on label).

blueprint_intent.approach: DBA-authored idempotent INSERT in a reviewed SQL file under an operator-gated ledger path; no migration runner involvement.
blueprint_intent.tests: throwaway-DB test applying schema skeleton + file twice, asserting one row

work_request_intent.compile_via: conduit plan (small, single-artifact) — this requirement is documentary and does not need a Blueprint parent

requirements.title: Replicate the recent resolution migrations to vanadium
requirements.outcome: V187, V219, V220 and V221 are replicated off-machine with matching checksums.
acceptance_criteria: The pg-backup run covering the four migrations exits 0 and its log names each one.
Per-table checksums for resolution.work_request, resolution.request_requirement_link and the V187-demoted views match between source and vanadium.
An R9 record cites the run id, timestamps and checksum output; any unreplicated item is named explicitly rather than implied.

blueprint_intent.approach: Reuse the existing pg-backup timer; add a verification step that asserts the four migration labels are present on the target.
blueprint_intent.tests: hermetic test over a fixture manifest, plus one live run recorded as evidence

requirements.title: Prove no reader depends on the dropped source_requirement shortcut
requirements.outcome: Every runtime reader of Requirement→WorkRequest provenance uses resolution.request_requirement_link, and a guard fails if the dropped column reappears in a query.
acceptance_criteria: A repo-wide search finds source_requirement_id only in migrations, historical docs, or explicit deprecation comments — never in a runtime query.
A hermetic guard test fails when a runtime query string references source_requirement_id.
The five previously identified consumer suites (moleculer routes, nebula-srv routes, cascade kg_impact, adonisjs harvest controller) pass unchanged.
evidence: guard test name and failing fixture

blueprint_intent.approach: Static scan over runtime source globs (excluding sql/ and docs/) wired into the existing guards job; allowlist entries require a deprecation comment on the same line.
blueprint_intent.tests: positive fixture (runtime query) fails; migration/docs fixture passes

specifications.title: WorkRequest dispatch runs without a human at the keyboard
specifications.goal: Turn the ratified queue from something a human starts into something that claims, executes and reduces work on its own, with evidence at each transition.
specifications.outcome: One queued WorkRequest is claimed, executed and completed by the loop, twice in a row, with receipts and no manual /run.
specifications.source: Analyst R2 Tier 2, including the 19 compiled drafts / 8 intent cards and the builder-grant / reviewer-ROLE_EXPIRED blockers.
specifications.scope_boundary: Admission and capability grants are ratified artifacts first; this Specification does not authorize batch admission of all drafts.

requirements.title: Ratify the derivation admission package
requirements.outcome: A Planner/Architect decision record accepts, amends or rejects the 19 drafts and 8 intent cards, with per-item disposition.
acceptance_criteria: Every draft and intent card has exactly one disposition (accept, amend, reject) in a single ratified artifact.
No resolution.work_request row and no Conduit plan is created by the ratification itself.
Accepted items name the WorkRequest they will become and the evidence that will close them.
evidence: row-count check proving zero new WRs

blueprint_intent.approach: Ratify as a document-level decision with a machine-readable disposition table, following the 46-row disposition precedent.
blueprint_intent.tests: verifier asserts 27 rows, one disposition each, no duplicate ids

requirements.title: Apply the builder grant and prove one claim
requirements.outcome: A builder capability grant is live and one QUEUED WorkRequest moves to EXECUTING under a lease and to COMPLETED with a receipt.
acceptance_criteria: The grant row exists with the ratified key set and is cited by record id.
A claim records actor, lease expiry and generation; a second concurrent claim is refused.
Completion writes a receipt naming the WorkRequest, the head sha and the verification that closed it.

blueprint_intent.approach: Grant application is DBA-owned; the claim path is exercised through the existing kernel with a single seeded WR and a negative concurrent claim.
blueprint_intent.tests: double-claim refusal; lease expiry sweep; receipt on completion

requirements.title: Renew reviewer admission and prove one review reduction
requirements.outcome: The reviewer's expired admission is resolved and a review request reduces to a review_judgement bound to a head sha.
acceptance_criteria: The ROLE_EXPIRED condition is cleared by a recorded decision, not by relaxing the check.
A REVIEW_REQUEST resolves to exactly one review_judgement citing head sha and the criteria it applied.
A stale-head review is refused with a structured reason.

blueprint_intent.approach: Re-grant through the capability path with a head-sha binding; add the stale-head negative test at the reducer boundary.
blueprint_intent.tests: stale head refused; self-review excluded; duplicate judgement impossible

requirements.title: Unattended dispatch drill
requirements.outcome: The scheduler claims and completes two consecutive WorkRequests with no manual /run, and a mid-claim kill leaves no orphaned lease.
acceptance_criteria: Three consecutive scheduler ticks produce exactly one claim per due WorkRequest.
Killing the runner mid-claim and restarting leaves the lease reclaimable after expiry and produces no duplicate execution.
The drill record cites both completions, the tick ids and the recovery evidence.

blueprint_intent.approach: Drive the existing night-shift scheduler in shadow mode against a seeded queue, then flip only for the drill window.
blueprint_intent.tests: idempotent tick test; orphan-lease recovery test

specifications.title: Migration ledger and worktree state are trustworthy
specifications.goal: Make the ledger a reliable preflight signal and stop the worktree backlog from hiding ready work.
specifications.outcome: Every verified-live migration has a ledger row, the preflight guard fails closed, and the worktree inventory is pruned to live branches only.
specifications.source: Analyst R2 Tier 3, re-verified: 38 ledger rows against 184 sql/V*.sql files; V187 is the only gap in V215-V221.
specifications.scope_boundary: Documentary backfill and inventory only. No migration is applied or reverted by this Specification.

requirements.title: Backfill documentary ledger entries for verified-live migrations
requirements.outcome: Every migration in V187-V214 that is verified live has exactly one ledger row citing its apply evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A generated coverage report lists each migration file, live-object evidence, and ledger status.
Each new row cites a merge commit or apply record and states whether the apply predates the ledger entry.
Re-running the backfill inserts nothing (idempotent).

blueprint_intent.approach: Generate a reviewed SQL batch from the coverage report; DBA applies under the ledger path; no migration runner.
blueprint_intent.tests: report correctness against a fixture schema; idempotency test

work_request_intent.deliverable: ledger coverage complete for the range

requirements.title: Fail-closed ledger preflight
requirements.outcome: Preflight refuses to proceed when a live schema object has no ledger row, and passes on the repaired state.
acceptance_criteria: With a deliberately unledgered live table, preflight exits non-zero and names the object.
On the repaired state it exits zero and prints the counted evidence.
Both behaviours are covered by a throwaway-DB test.

blueprint_intent.approach: Compare information_schema objects introduced by migration files against ledger labels; unknown provenance fails closed.
blueprint_intent.tests: throwaway DB with one unledgered table fails; repaired DB passes

requirements.title: Worktree and branch inventory with a safe prune
requirements.outcome: The 82-worktree backlog is inventoried with merge status, and only merged, clean worktrees are pruned.
acceptance_criteria: The inventory lists every worktree with branch, merge status, dirty state and associated PR.
Prune refuses any dirty worktree or unmerged branch and reports why.
Before/after counts and the exact pruned list are recorded.

blueprint_intent.approach: Read git worktree list + gh pr list; delete only when merged and clean; dry-run by default.

specifications.title: Ingestion and infrastructure drift are closed
specifications.goal: Restore transcript ingestion and make the deployment manifest agree with what is actually running.
specifications.outcome: Absorb is ingesting again, WAL/PITR posture is decided and recorded, and Terrain no longer reports services offline while they answer.
specifications.source: Analyst R2 Tier 4, including the WAL deadline, the 7 thallium services and the two absorb worktrees.
specifications.scope_boundary: Configuration and deployment repair only. No new service is introduced and no data model changes.

requirements.title: Decide and record WAL/PITR posture
requirements.outcome: archive_mode and archive_command are recorded, and either PITR is proven by a restore test or its absence is explicitly accepted with a dated decision.
acceptance_criteria: SHOW archive_mode / archive_command output is recorded.
If archiving is enabled, a restore-to-timestamp test succeeds and is cited.
If it remains off, a decision record names the risk owner and a revisit date.

blueprint_intent.approach: Configuration audit first; restore rehearsal on a throwaway instance; decision record either way.
blueprint_intent.tests: restore rehearsal checklist with named target database (Ruling 29)

requirements.title: Reconcile Terrain manifest with live probes
requirements.outcome: The 7 thallium services' manifest state matches their probe result, and the IPv6 probe misconfiguration is fixed.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest state and probe state agree for all 7 services.
nexus-console, nebula-ui and cascade-ui probe over the configured address family and report UP.
The topology view shows zero false-OFFLINE entries.

blueprint_intent.approach: Fix probe address resolution, then update manifest rows to observed state with a validator that fails on disagreement.
blueprint_intent.deliverable: probe config change + manifest reconciliation script

requirements.title: Resume transcript ingestion
requirements.outcome: The absorb timeout and model fixes are landed and a new transcript is ingested end to end.
acceptance_criteria: Both absorb worktrees are merged or explicitly closed with a reason.
A transcript posted after deployment appears in the transcripts surface.
Ingestion lag is below 24h at the time of verification.

blueprint_intent.approach: Land the two existing fixes, then prove ingestion with a single known transcript rather than a bulk replay.
blueprint_intent.tests: absorb unit tests + one live ingestion check

specifications.title: Service inventory is bound to the semantic spine
specifications.goal: Give the service estate one canonical, deterministic binding to assets, and resume the promotion path that feeds the cockpit.
specifications.outcome: The unmapped services are bound or queued with reasons, the Stage-3 promotion pipeline runs again, and one SOLScript widget is proven end to end.
specifications.source: Analyst R2 Tier 5, including 36/102 unbound services, the 0/25 stage-0 score and the throttler convergence goal.
specifications.scope_boundary: Binding and one pilot widget. Do not attempt the full cockpit convergence in this Specification.

requirements.title: Deterministic service→asset binding
requirements.outcome: Unmapped Terrain services are bound by a deterministic rule or queued for review with a stated reason.
acceptance_criteria: A binding report accounts for all 102 services: bound, queued, or excluded with reason.
No binding is created below the declared similarity floor; below-floor cases go to the review queue.
Re-running the binder is idempotent.

blueprint_intent.approach: Deterministic name/path rules first; embedding similarity only as a ranked suggestion, never as an automatic bind.

requirements.title: Resume the Stage-3 promotion pipeline
requirements.outcome: One promotion run completes with a receipt and no manual database writes.
acceptance_criteria: A promotion run produces a receipt naming inputs, gate results and outputs.
No row is written outside the promotion service's canonical path.
The run is reproducible from the receipt alone.

blueprint_intent.approach: Unblock the halted pipeline rather than rebuilding it; add the write-audit check as the acceptance instrument.

requirements.title: First SOLScript-backed throttler widget
requirements.outcome: One of nebula-*, barbie or atlas-ui renders from a SOLScript contract instead of imperative fetch logic, with parity evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The widget's data comes from one SOLScript contract with no parallel hand-written fetch path.
Old and new render the same data for a fixed fixture (parity test).
Removing the legacy path does not change the rendered output.

blueprint_intent.approach: Pick the smallest widget, express its projection as a SOLScript contract, keep the legacy path behind a flag until parity passes.

work_request_intent.deliverable: one widget on the semantic spine

open_decision.question: Which Requirement surface is canonical for the Specification/Blueprint/WorkRequest chain: port nebula.requirements into resolution.requirement (P4a), or declare nebula.requirements canonical and retarget V220's FK (P4b)?
open_decision.why_it_blocks: P1/P2/P3/P5 all reference Requirements. With resolution.requirement at 0 rows and the live 27 in nebula, either choice is a real authority move with migration consequences; neither can be inferred from the code.

options.label: Port into resolution.requirement (matches V220 and the canonical landing)
options.cost: identity-preserving port of 27 rows + nebula-srv read/write repoint + compatibility view window
options.benefit: one authority, existing link tables become usable as designed

options.label: Declare nebula.requirements canonical and retarget the link FKs
options.cost: V220 FK retarget migration + diverges from plan 8261650's declared target
options.benefit: no data port; smaller immediate change

open_decision.recommendation: P4a, because V220/V221 already landed on the resolution side and a second retarget would re-open the cutover plan 8261650 just closed.

non_goals: No schema mutation or migration apply in this artifact
No Requirement, Specification, Blueprint or WorkRequest row creation
No claim that the Analyst's unverified figures are measured facts (see captured_state.analyst_claims_not_reverified_here)
